heroHeadline: Ukraine Launches 347-Drone Retaliation After Russia Violates Ceasefire 1,820 Times; Dueling Truces Collapse
heroSubtitle: Ukraine fired its second-largest aerial attack of the war overnight May 6–7 — 347 drones across 20+ Russian regions including Moscow — in direct retaliation for Russia's wholesale violation of Ukraine's declared ceasefire. Zelensky reported 1,820 Russian ceasefire violations in just 10 hours (nearly 30 assault operations, 20+ airstrikes using 70+ guided glide bombs), killing 22 and wounding 82 overnight May 5–6. The dueling truce proposals — Russia's Victory Day ceasefire (May 8–9) vs. Ukraine's open-ended offer — both collapsed almost immediately. On May 5, Russia had killed 27 across Ukraine in a mass strike using 11 Iskander-M missiles + 164 drones, hitting Naftogaz gas facilities in a deliberately double-strike on rescue workers. Ukraine struck back strategically: Flamingo cruise missiles (1,500+ km range) halted Russia's largest oil refinery in Kirishi, Leningrad Oblast — 3 of 4 crude distillation units destroyed — and hit a Cheboksary military factory producing precision-weapon components (2 killed, 32 injured). Russia's scaled-down Victory Day parade on May 9 will again feature no military vehicles. Russian personnel losses now exceed 1.338 million.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OHCHR, ISW, CSIS, Ukrainian MoD, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, EU Council, UK MoD, and major news outlets including Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Euronews, and RBC-Ukraine. Casualty figures are estimates; Russia has never released official figures.
